text: In Agile methodology, software is built through iterative development. Instead of delivering one massive final product, teams work in short, focused cycles called sprints, which typically last two to four weeks. Each sprint begins by selecting tasks from a prioritized list known as the backlog. These tasks are broken down into small, practical units called user stories, which describe a feature from the user's perspective. To track progress, the team holds a brief daily meeting, or standup, where each member shares what they did yesterday, what they will do today, and any obstacles they face. This constant feedback loop allows the team to adapt quickly to changes and deliver value continuously.
